We buy Kansas City houses as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who bills what in Kansas City

  • Jackson County Assessment Department handles assessment.

Local notes

Behind on Kansas City property tax?

Get My Cash Offer →

Kansas City by the numbers

Which county bills my Kansas City, Missouri property tax?

It depends on which side of the city your house is on. Kansas City covers about 319 square miles across four counties: Jackson, Clay, Platte and Cass (Wikipedia). The city does not send its own bill. Its finance page says every taxable parcel is assessed by the county assessor and the city levy appears on the county bill.

  • Jackson County: Collection Department, 816-881-3232.
  • Clay County: Collector, 816-407-3200.
  • Platte and Cass counties: look up the county collector on that county's official site, using your parcel number or address.

The county named on your last tax statement tells you which office to call.

What does Kansas City's own levy look like?

The city lists five levies, each stated per $100 of assessed valuation. The 2024 combined figure on the finance page is $1.5291 for city purposes. Other districts add their own levies, so ask the collector for the full rate on your parcel.

City of Kansas City levies, tax year 2024 (kcmo.gov finance page)
Levy2024 rate per $100
General purpose$0.5469
Health$0.3799
Health temporary$0.1672
Museum$0.0151
Debt service$0.4200

Missouri assesses residential property at 19 percent of true value, agricultural land at 12 percent, other real property at 32 percent and personal property at 33 1/3 percent. Each county assessor adjusts real property values in odd-numbered years, so a new reassessment lands in 2027.

What does Kansas City look like for a house seller?

By population and by area Kansas City leads Missouri, and it stands at the confluence of the Kansas and Missouri rivers. It began as a river landing, and the town of Kansas was incorporated on June 1, 1850 before taking the name Kansas City in 1889. River Market, 18th and Vine and Country Club Plaza are among its best known districts. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts give 521,220 residents for 2025 and 221,979 households. Owners hold 55.4% of homes. The median owner-occupied value is $242,900, median gross rent is $1,238 and median household income is $69,166.

No single school district covers the city. About 15 separate districts serve it, so two houses a few blocks apart can sit in different school districts. The economy leans on federal offices, a Federal Reserve bank, an IRS service center and a Honeywell plant, plus animal health research and agriculture companies such as Dairy Farmers of America.

Weather is part of the picture for any house here. The city sits in Tornado Alley, and it has had ice storms and river flooding. Wind, hail and water damage are realistic repair items for an older house here, and a seller facing both repairs and a tax bill can weigh an as-is sale.

Why can a Kansas City levy change from year to year?

The city's finance page explains that a Missouri constitutional amendment caps the total tax the city may impose in a fiscal year. Levies are set to bring in about the same revenue as the year before, and a majority vote is needed to go past that limit. Value from new construction, new personal property and newly annexed areas sits outside the cap.

Each levy also has a ceiling. The general purpose levy tops out at $1.0000 per $100 and the 2024 rate was $0.5469. The health levy has a $0.5000 maximum against $0.3799 charged. A reassessment can therefore move your assessed value without moving the rate, and a rate can move while your value stays flat.

When is Jackson County property tax due, and how do I pay?

The 2026 bill is due in full by December 31, 2026. The county's Board of Equalization FAQ adds that recalculations for 2026 appeal decisions are suspended until January 2027, so the bill still has to be paid on time. Any refund is then issued automatically, and paying under protest is not required to get one. When a mortgage company pays the bill, a refund goes back to the lender.

  • In person: Jackson County Courthouse, 415 E 12th Street in Kansas City, or the Truman Courthouse, 112 W Lexington Avenue in Independence, open weekdays from 8 to 5.
  • Drop boxes at both courthouses close at midnight on December 31. Cash does not go in them.
  • By mail to the Jackson County Collector. The postmark must be December 31 or earlier.
  • Online at payments.jacksongov.org. E-check costs $1.25. Cards cost 2.75% of the bill, and a $2 per transaction fee applies, all kept by the processor.

The county accepts partial payments on real property, but they cannot be made online. Interest, penalties and fees accrue on the unpaid part after December 31. Seniors may split the county bill into four equal installments without penalty through the Senior Quad Payment Program, and the Collection Department can say whether your account qualifies.

What can I do about a Jackson County assessment now?

The county's appeal board, the Board of Equalization, took 2026 filings through July 13, 2026, and that date has passed. For a notice or print summary of values, call the Real Property Assessment Department at 816-881-3530 or email tpaASMT@jacksongov.org.

After the board rules, you can appeal to the Missouri State Tax Commission, which has its own online process. Two points from the board's FAQ matter. Signing a stipulated value from the Assessment Department cancels the board appeal and ends any Commission appeal. A withdrawal must be in writing, and the board's mailing address is 1300 Washington, Kansas City, MO 64106.

Taxes paid under protest follow Missouri statute 139.031: full payment on time plus a written statement of grounds and the claimed fair market value. The county sends protest payments to Attn: Protest, P.O. Box 219747, Kansas City, MO 64121-9747. Protest funds are released every other month, so a refund tied to a value change usually comes faster without it.

What if my Kansas City house sits in Clay County?

Clay County's Collector says tax bills normally go out by mid-November, and an owner who has not received one by November 30 should call 816-407-3200. Missouri law requires payment by December 31 whether or not a bill arrives.

A payment postmarked after December 31 draws a one-time 9% penalty and interest of 1.5% per month on the unpaid balance. Clay County asks owners not to rely on bank bill-pay services, since those payments often reach the office without a postmark and are posted by the date on the check. Debit cards and e-check are free to Clay County customers, and credit cards carry a 2.45% fee.

How should I handle a tax bill when selling a Kansas City house?

Start with the county, parcel number and bill year. The title company asks the collector for the amount owed and pays it at closing. If a house has an old year unpaid plus a current bill, getting the payoff in writing before you sign anything avoids surprises on the settlement statement.

A homeowner who owes back tax and has repairs to make can also sell the house as-is for cash. In that case the title company pays the tax from the proceeds, as it would in any other sale.

More questions about Kansas City, MO Property Tax Guide

Who bills property tax for a house in Kansas City, Missouri?

The county where the parcel sits. Kansas City spans Jackson, Clay, Platte and Cass counties, and the city's levy is added to the county bill rather than billed separately.

When is the 2026 Kansas City tax bill due?

December 31, 2026. In Jackson County the drop boxes close at midnight that day and mailed payments need a postmark of that date or earlier.

Can I still appeal my 2026 Jackson County value?

No. The Board of Equalization deadline was July 13, 2026. Call 816-881-3530 for a value summary and watch for the next reassessment in 2027.

Do I have to pay under protest to get a refund in Jackson County?

No. The county says refunds from a value change are issued automatically. Paying under protest can delay them, because protest funds are released every other month.

What is the Kansas City city property tax rate?

The city's combined 2024 levy was $1.5291 per $100 of assessed valuation. School and other district rates are added on the county bill, so ask your collector for the total on your parcel.

Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Springfield, MO Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Springfield, MO Property Tax Guide sale

Owe Springfield Property Tax? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Springfield houses as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who bills what in Springfield

  • Greene County Assessor handles assessment.

Due dates

Due date not stated on the opened Collector home page; Missouri taxes are generally due December 31 (not confirmed on a Greene page).. See the official page.

Challenging your assessment

Optional informal appeal with the Assessor (417-868-4101, propertyappeals@greenecountymo.gov); formal BOE appeal form must reach the County Clerk by the second Monday in July (July 13, 2026) by email boe@greenecountymo.gov or mail; State Tax Commission appeal by September 30 or 30 days after BOE action, whichever is later.. See the official page.

Local notes

  • Greene County Assessor is an elected official (Brent Johnson per page); Collector page names Allen Icet.
  • BOE is administered through the County Clerk.
  • Census Vintage 2025 population 169847; county per Census SUMLEV 157: Greene County.
Behind on Springfield property tax?
We buy Springfield houses as-is, and the title company pays unpaid tax from the proceeds.
Get My Cash Offer →

Springfield by the numbers

Which office handles property tax on a Springfield house?

Greene County handles it, not City Hall. Three county offices split the work: an elected Assessor sets the value, the Clerk turns the levies into the annual tax book, and the Collector of Revenue mails the statement and takes the payment.

  • Assessor: Brent Johnson, 940 N. Boonville Avenue, Room 35. The real estate line is (417) 868-4101.
  • Collector of Revenue: Allen Icet, Room 109 of the Historic Courthouse, (417) 868-4036. The counter is open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., closed on holidays.
  • County Clerk: keeps the levy rates and acts as secretary to the Board of Equalization, (417) 829-6244.

Owner, school district and taxing district for any parcel can be looked up on the county's Public Access site, which refreshes every night.

What kind of city is Springfield for a seller?

Springfield is Missouri's third largest city and the biggest in the Ozarks, with a Census estimate of 169,847 people in July 2025 spread over roughly 82 square miles of the Springfield Plateau. Health care, manufacturing, retail, education and tourism carry the economy. Wikipedia names CoxHealth and Mercy as the biggest employers, and Bass Pro Shops, O'Reilly Auto Parts and Jack Henry keep headquarters here.

Missouri State, Drury, Evangel and Ozarks Technical Community College all have campuses in or near the center of town. City government follows a council-manager model, with eight council members and a mayor on four-year terms.

Springfield by the Census numbers
MeasureSpringfield
Residents, July 2025 estimate169,847
Homes lived in by their owners, 2020-202443.9%
Typical owner-reported home value$177,700
Median rent$964
Median household income$49,311
Share below the poverty line18.4%
Average trip to work17.6 minutes

Owners live in only 43.9 percent of Springfield homes, and the typical home value is well under the $306,700 reported for University City or the $331,300 for Wentzville.

What is the deadline to pay Springfield property tax?

The deadline is midnight on December 31. Greene County's notice on the 2025 bills warned of a 9 percent penalty plus 2 percent interest after that date, and said a mailed bank check must be postmarked December 31 or earlier. Expect the 2026 statement around the middle of November; the 2025 notice told anyone without a mailed copy by Thanksgiving to write to collectorhelp@greenecountymo.gov.

  • Pay at CountyCollector.com, by mail, by phone, or at the Room 109 counter in the courthouse at 940 N. Boonville Avenue.
  • The Collector's page lists processor charges of $1.00 for an e-check, 1.5 percent on a debit card and 2.3 percent on a credit card, with a $2.00 minimum.
  • A hallway drop box takes payments during business hours until year end.
  • When several years are owed, the oldest has to be cleared before any newer bill.

Anything unpaid is delinquent from January 1. The Collector's office is closed on Thanksgiving Day and the Friday after, so do not plan an in-person payment that week.

Who pays the tax when a Springfield house sells mid-year?

Whoever owns the house on the day the bill is due answers for it. The Collector's real estate page explains that the tax attaches to the parcel, that the office does not split a bill between sellers and buyers, and that the closing company normally credits the seller's share to the buyer. Read the settlement statement line by line to see that credit.

Where a lender pays taxes from escrow, the statement goes to the lender. If the lender misses a mid-December payment, the bill is remailed to the owner with extra time. After a payoff, the Collector does not need a call, but the mailing address on file with the Assessor should be current.

  • Get the balance for this year and any older years from the title company before choosing a closing day.
  • Make sure the owner name in the Assessor's record matches the recorded deed.
  • Save the receipt, which can be downloaded from the Collector's site after an online payment.

How can I challenge a Springfield property valuation?

Missouri has the Assessor set new real estate values as of January 1 of every odd-numbered year, so the next full reassessment lands in 2027. Value change notices usually go out before June, and in 2025 they were mailed the second full week of May. Only owners whose value rose get one.

  • Informal review: call an appraiser on the dedicated phone lines named in the notice, or use the Assessor's informal appeal form for real property.
  • Board of Equalization: forms must reach the County Clerk by the second Monday in July. For 2026 that was July 13, so the window has closed.
  • State Tax Commission: the last stop, reachable at 573-751-2414.

The Board has eight citizen members, three named by the Greene County Commission and five by the City of Springfield. It meets at 9:00 a.m. on the second Tuesday of each month to certify corrections to the tax book, and holds the formal July hearings in Room 212 of the Historic Courthouse. It may raise, lower or leave a value alone.

The Assessor stresses that value is only one input. Multiply the assessed value by the district levy and divide by 100 to get the bill, which means a higher levy can lift a bill whose value stayed flat.

Which tax relief and tax sale rules should a Springfield owner know?

The county's Senior Tax Credit lowers real estate tax for eligible older homeowners. New applicants may enroll from January 2 to June 30, and an approved household stays in without yearly renewal unless ownership or occupancy changes. A delinquent real estate balance on June 30 removes a participant, and the credit never moves the December 31 deadline.

Tax sales come next for owners who stay behind. Greene County auctions qualifying parcels on the fourth Monday of August at 10 a.m. in Room 212 of the Historic Courthouse. A parcel qualifies when two or more years are owed on May 1, and paying everything owed before the sale takes it off the list. A Notice of Impending Sale goes out in April, and from July 1 the office accepts only certified funds.

Owners who plan to sell while behind should phone the Collector early and request the exact payoff, because the figure changes as interest accrues.

Do Springfield city rules affect rentals and short-term stays?

Yes. Springfield defines a short-term rental as any stay under 30 consecutive days and requires registration and a license under City Code Section 36-473. A Type 1 license covers a home where the operator lives and needs an annual business license. A Type 2 covers a home the operator does not live in, within single-family and townhouse districts, and needs a permit plus a neighborhood meeting. No Type 2 may sit within 500 feet of another.

The Type 2 application costs $715 for planning review and $30 for inspection, plus the business license. A buyer hoping to run stays at your address should confirm with the city that the property qualifies before the offer goes firm. The city's zoning also caps unrelated occupants at three in single-family and townhouse districts and four in the multifamily districts.

More questions about Springfield, MO Property Tax Guide

What day is Springfield property tax due?

December 31. Greene County's 2025 notice described a 9 percent penalty and 2 percent interest after that date, and a mailed check needs a December 31 postmark or earlier.

Which phone number reaches the Springfield tax collector?

The Greene County Collector answers at (417) 868-4036 about payments, and the Assessor at (417) 868-4101 about values. The collection counter is in Room 109 of the Historic Courthouse.

Does Greene County split the tax bill between buyer and seller?

No. The Collector does not divide bills, so the closing company usually credits the seller's share to the buyer. Check the settlement statement.

Is it too late to dispute my 2026 Springfield value?

The Board of Equalization deadline was July 13, 2026, so formal appeals for this year have closed. The next reassessment arrives in 2027.

When does Greene County auction delinquent property?

On the fourth Monday of August, at 10 a.m. in Room 212 of the Historic Courthouse. Parcels owing at least two years on May 1 qualify.

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Independence, MO Property Tax Guide sale

Owe Independence Property Tax? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Independence houses as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who bills what in Independence

  • Jackson County Assessment Department handles assessment.

Local notes

Behind on Independence property tax?
We buy Independence houses as-is, and the title company pays unpaid tax from the proceeds.
Get My Cash Offer →

Independence by the numbers

Who sends an Independence, MO property tax bill?

The City of Independence does not bill real estate tax on its own. Jackson County does, through two departments: Assessment sets the value, and Collection sends the bill and takes the money. Independence owners can pay at the Historic Truman Courthouse, 112 W Lexington Ave, Suite 114, or at the Jackson County Courthouse in Kansas City. Both open at 8:00 a.m. and close at 5:00 p.m. on weekdays, skipping county holidays.

Call Collection at (816) 881-3232 or write Collections@jacksongov.org. To correct a name or mailing address on a real property account, phone Assessment at 816-881-3530. A change of address filed with the post office or the Missouri DMV never reaches the tax account. Phone lines run long in November and December, so email or the county's online account lookup may be faster for simple questions.

When is the next Independence bill due, and what will it cost to pay?

The tax year 2026 deadline is December 31, 2026, a little over six weeks from today. Last year the county printed bills in early November and finished mailing on December 12. It tells owners without a bill by December 8 to call, and it warns that a bill that never came is no defense. A check must carry a USPS postmark dated December 31 or earlier, and the county suggests posting it days early because post office drop boxes sometimes stamp the next day.

The Truman Courthouse drop box, at the south door, locks at midnight on the last day, and cash does not belong in it. The county ran extra Saturday morning hours in the weeks before the 2025 deadline, so look for a 2026 schedule on its Collection page.

Jackson County online payment charges, from the 2025 Collection FAQ
ItemCharge
Any online payment$2.00 flat
E-check (ACH)plus $1.25
Debit or credit cardplus 2.75%
Check or money orderMade out to Jackson County Collector, with the account number

Those charges go to the payment processor, since the county says it keeps none of them. The online system stops at 11:40 p.m. on December 31.

How does a sale affect the tax bill on an Independence house?

Jackson County describes the tax as a lien that follows the real estate, which means a buyer inherits any unpaid real estate tax. Its FAQ adds that buyer and seller commonly prorate the year at closing and that a closing company may settle whatever is due if it knows the amount. As a rule nobody pays the Collector on the day of the sale.

  • A buyer who receives a credit at closing should confirm it is meant for the coming tax bill.
  • The new bill may still go out under the seller's name until the buyer reports ownership and an address to the Assessor.
  • Homes with escrow accounts need the bill forwarded to the lender.

Check the parcel at payments.jacksongov.org before you list. Prior-year balances land on the current statement as one lump, so keep last year's bill if you need the breakdown.

Is it too late to contest an Independence value for 2026?

The Board of Equalization took filings from May 1 through July 13, 2026, and that window is shut. The Board now meets at 1300 Washington in Kansas City. Owners who already filed can withdraw in writing whenever they like.

A decision reached before December will not reach this year's statement. Jackson County says it paused recalculation of 2026 appeals and stipulations until January 2027, so the full 2026 amount should be paid by December 31, 2026. Any overpayment comes back as an automatic refund with no protest needed. Partial payments on real estate are accepted but cannot be made online, and interest and fees still apply to the unpaid remainder.

The next level is the State Tax Commission, which runs its own online application. An owner who signed the Assessor's stipulation has already closed the Board case and cannot proceed to the Commission.

What kind of city is Independence, Missouri?

Independence lies on the south bank of the Missouri River, covering roughly 78 square miles, most of it in Jackson County with a small piece in Clay County. Founded on March 29, 1827, it served as an outfitting point for the Santa Fe, California and Oregon trails. Harry S. Truman grew up in town, and his library and home site draw visitors. The 2020 census counted 123,011 residents, fifth among Missouri cities.

  • July 1, 2025 estimate: 121,675 people
  • Households (2020 to 2024): 51,477 averaging 2.34 people
  • Share of homes occupied by owners: 60.9%
  • Median owner-occupied home value: $172,900
  • Median gross rent: $1,109
  • Median household income: $60,339
  • Average commute: 23.9 minutes

All of the figures above come from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts table for the city. Visitors come for the National Frontier Trails Museum, the Vaile Mansion and the Midwest Genealogy Center, and the Labor Day festival Santa-Cali-Gon Days has run continuously since 1973. Mid-Continent Public Library runs three branches in the city, the Kansas City Public Library operates its Trails West Branch here, and Graceland University has an Independence campus.

What do schools and roads mean for an Independence listing?

Independence, Blue Springs, Fort Osage and Raytown each have school district territory inside the city, so buyers ask which district a particular street falls under. The parcel record answers that. Three public high schools and four public middle schools stand within the city, and Blue River Community College is part of the Metropolitan Community College system.

Interstate 70 links the city with Kansas City, Columbia and St. Louis, I-435 skirts its western edge and I-470 follows Route 291 south toward Lee's Summit. US 24 runs along the northern border and US 40 along part of the southern one. Routes 7, 12, 78 and 291 fill in the rest. The city owns its electric utility, Independence Power and Light, founded in 1901. A 2016 city financial report named the Independence School District (2,200 employees), Northrop Grumman Innovation Systems (1,722) and Centerpoint Medical Center (1,400) as top employers.

Why do Independence owners care about the county's assessment record?

In September 2023 the Independence City Council voted to sue Jackson County, citing inconsistent and unfair assessment practices, and engaged outside counsel to file the case. For appeals, RSMo 137.115 says that where a charter county's valuation came from a computer-assisted method, the assessor must back it with appraisal-based findings and the prices of at least three comparable sales within a mile.

Owners who plan a future challenge should start gathering their own evidence now. The Board's appeal page lists certified appraisals, sale contracts and settlement statements, repair estimates and, for income property, rent rolls and leases. It states that a real estate agent's opinion does not qualify, and that evidence on a phone or tablet will not be considered at the hearing.

More questions about Independence, MO Property Tax Guide

Which office collects Independence property tax?

Jackson County's Collection Department, at the Historic Truman Courthouse in Independence or the Kansas City courthouse. Call (816) 881-3232.

What is the payment deadline for tax year 2026?

December 31, 2026. Mailed payments need that postmark or an earlier one, and the online system accepts payments until 11:40 p.m. that night.

Do buyers or sellers settle the Independence tax bill?

They usually prorate the year at closing, according to Jackson County, and a closing company may pay any amount already due. The buyer is liable for unpaid real estate tax because it follows the property.

Can a pending appeal lower the 2026 bill before it is due?

No. Recalculations are suspended until January 2027, so pay the whole 2026 bill by December 31 and a refund follows automatically if the value drops.

What surcharge applies to online tax payments in Independence?

A $2.00 fee per transaction, plus $1.25 for e-checks or 2.75 percent for cards. The county reports that it receives none of these fees.
